newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro shares hold early gains, dollar drifts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro shares hold early gains, dollar drifts.

text.p: European shares mostly held on to earlier gains on Friday afternoon, although they came under pressure when Wall Street failed to build on its 30th closing high of the year.

On the foreign exchanges, the dollar drifted off earlier highs as a short-lived boost from increased political uncertainty in Russia faded, although it was well supported above 1.54 marks, dealers said.

The Dow Jones industrial average made a tentative start but soon headed lower and was down around 14 points by 1415 GMT after data showed that the U.S. trade deficit narrowed in August but was still wider than expected.
The total trade deficit on goods and services fell to $10.83 billion in August from $11.6 billion in July.
Meanwhile, the fear of political upheaval in Russia following President Boris Yeltsin's sacking of security chief Alexander Lebed was a diminishing influence.

Europe's leading share markets advanced in early trading but then stalled. By mid-afternoon, London's FTSE 100 index was holding on to a gain of 0.4 percent, just shy of its record high, while the French and German bourses were up 0.7 and 0.6 percent, respectively.

In London, shares sagged from their opening highs after the latest batch of British monetary data lent support to calls for an interest rate rise. September M4 money supply rose a stronger-than-expected 0.8 percent in the month.
But the government bond market remained firm and continued to lend some support to the share market's gains.
"The market is still positive but the trend is not that firm," said Tom Pelc, technical analyst at MMS International. "We can still go higher but the move will be more gradual."

French shares touched a high for the year of 2,187.05 points on the CAC-40 index but then edged back. German shares ended floor trade at a record close of 2,734.82 on the 30-share DAX index, although off an earlier intra-day high of 2,737.51.

Economists said the idea that the German economy was more exposed than other Western economies at times of Russian political stress -- in both geographical and trade terms -- held less significance than it used to do.
Klaus Baader, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said Russia's relations with the West were on a much more multilateral basis, compared with the early 1990s.

Some superstitious investors across Europe were wary of the approach of Saturday's anniversary of the 1987 stock market crash. October features heavily in stock market jitters, also being the month of the 1929 Wall Street crash.

The dollar was robust against the yen in early trading and set a fresh 33-month high at 112.63 amid a renewed bout of yen weakness ahead of the U.S. trade data and the Japanese general election on Sunday.
CURRENCIES AT 1415 GMT
The dollar was trading at 1.5420 marks and 112.55 yen compared with 1.5436 and 112.25 in late European business on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1415 GMT
London - The FTSE index was up 11.1 points at 4,053.2.
Frankfurt - The 30-share DAX index closed floor trade up 18.56 points at 2,734.82. The Ibis DAX stood at 2,723, up 6.10 points, in post-bourse electronic trading.
Paris - The CAC-40 share index was up 16.41 points at 2,181.74.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $380.00 an ounce, up from the morning fix of $379.60 and after closing on Thursday in Europe at $380.45.
